angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 917,628 km at 11.13 pc = 1.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 89.88 +/- 0.23 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 11.126 +/- 0.028 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 89.6850 +/- 0.1638 mas (same row, RUWE 3.17), 547.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.319 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.103 +/- 0.009 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.319 +/- 0.011 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 917,628 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.138 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.138 +/- 0.01 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6157 +/- 37 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6157 +/- 37 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 16895: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6157 +/- 37 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/theta-persei.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.254, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * tet Per: spectral type F8V (1981ApJS...45..437A)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * tet Per: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
luminositySource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 438829629114680704, flags_flame 00: lum_flame 2.3408136 solar luminosities (16th to 84th percentiles 2.3301818 to 2.3504896); its log10 is recorded
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 438829629114680704, flags_flame 00: age_flame 2.774404 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 2.1767707 to 3.3722296)
